subject.title: fix(plugins): plugins.deny is bypassed by a mixed-case manifest id

question: Should plugin policy IDs be globally case-insensitive identities, or should only negative deny/reserved checks fold case while positive allow and trust checks remain fail-closed?
rationale: The patch must choose a stable authorization identity contract: positive case-folding is safe only if discovery rejects case-folded collisions, while negative-only folding preserves existing fail-closed allowlist behavior.

options.title: Reject folded collisions
options.body: Keep case-insensitive policy matching but reject or disable later discoveries whose declared IDs collide after case folding, preserving one authorization identity per policy key.

options.title: Fold negative checks only
options.body: Normalize deny and reserved-ID checks while leaving allowlist, explicit enablement, and owner-trust comparisons fail-closed for mixed-case IDs.

recommendation.title: Reject folded collisions
recommendation.body: Keep case-insensitive policy matching but reject or disable later discoveries whose declared IDs collide after case folding, preserving one authorization identity per policy key.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to plugin loader, contract, and boundary behavior needed to settle the identity invariant.
